chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Burned out by nightlife; trouble with the horn
summary: Overindulging in romance and late nights, Butler woke one morning unable to get a sound from his trumpet; his doctor said he was just worn out.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So I'm up there and I'm hearing that going on, you know, feeling good, happy. But I was having too much romance. Oh, romance was something else. I never had so much romance. One morning I picked that horn up and didn't nothing come out. Didn't nothing come out. I said, Oh, my goodness. I went to the doctor and he said well, where do you work?" and I said, I work two sets, and you come off there 8:00 o'clock, 9:00 o'clock, 10:00 o'clock, 11:00 o'clock. And you start at 11:00 o'clock at night. Well, I would be sporting all day long and all night long. He said, well, you're just worn out, that's all. So he gave me some pills and medicine and everything and I
got myself back together. So I was sort of cooling.
